models.name: Stable Diffusion 3
models.architecture: Rectified-flow MM-DiT in a 16-channel autoencoder latent space, with separate text and image weights joined in attention and conditioned on CLIP-L/14, OpenCLIP bigG/14 and T5-XXL
models.notes: Text tokens (CLIP penultimate states padded and concatenated with T5-XXL tokens) and 2×2-patched latent tokens are concatenated into one sequence; each MM-DiT block keeps separate modulation, projection and MLP weights per modality but runs one joint attention (paper Figure 2). Timestep and pooled CLIP embeddings drive adaLN-style modulation; optional RMSNorm on Q and K stabilizes high-resolution training. Training uses rectified flow with logit-normal timestep sampling. The paper scales the model by depth d (hidden size 64·d) up to d = 38, about 8B parameters, and shows T5 can be dropped at inference at some cost to typography. SD3 Medium (June 2024) was the first open release. Per the SD3.5 Medium model card, Medium uses MMDiT-X, which adds self-attention modules to the first transformer layers; SD3.5 Large Turbo is a 4-step distilled Large model.
models.description: Stable Diffusion 3 is Stability AI's third-generation text-to-image family and the paper that introduced the MM-DiT backbone. Instead of injecting text through cross-attention, it treats text and image latents as two token streams with their own weights that meet in a shared attention operation, trained with a rectified-flow objective and a noise-schedule sampling that favours intermediate timesteps. Three frozen text encoders (two CLIP models and T5-XXL) provide both a pooled vector for modulation and a token sequence for the joint attention. The architecture was scaled to 8B parameters in the paper and released as SD3 Medium and later as the SD3.5 Large, Large Turbo and Medium checkpoints.

sources.title: Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis

models.name: StackGAN
models.architecture: Two-stage conditional GAN: a Stage-I generator sketches a 64×64 image from text and noise, and a Stage-II encoder–residual–decoder generator refines it to 256×256 conditioned on the text again
models.notes: Introduces Conditioning Augmentation: the conditioning vector is sampled from a Gaussian whose mean and diagonal covariance are predicted from the pretrained text embedding, with a KL regularizer toward the standard normal. Stage II takes no noise vector; it downsamples the Stage-I image, concatenates the spatially replicated text conditioning and applies residual blocks before upsampling (paper Figure 2). Both stages use matching-aware discriminators. Evaluated on CUB, Oxford-102 and MS COCO. The official repository is a TensorFlow implementation and links a separate PyTorch implementation.

sources.title: StackGAN: Text to Photo-realistic Image Synthesis with Stacked Generative Adversarial Networks

models.name: StackGAN++ (StackGAN-v2)
models.architecture: End-to-end tree-structured GAN whose shared trunk branches into generators at 64×64, 128×128 and 256×256, each paired with its own discriminator
models.notes: For text-to-image, the conditioning vector (from Conditioning Augmentation on the text embedding) and noise feed the first stage, and the conditioning vector is re-injected at each later branch. Discriminators are trained jointly on unconditional (real/fake) and conditional (image–text match) losses, and a color-consistency regularizer ties the scales together (paper Fig. 2). The same framework is also used for unconditional generation on LSUN and ImageNet. The TPAMI paper also presents the two-stage StackGAN (StackGAN-v1), catalogued separately as StackGAN.

sources.title: StackGAN++: Realistic Image Synthesis with Stacked Generative Adversarial Networks

models.name: TAC-GAN
models.architecture: AC-GAN variant conditioned on Skip-Thought text embeddings, whose discriminator predicts both real/fake and the image class
models.notes: A fully connected network maps the Skip-Thought caption embedding to a latent vector that is concatenated with noise and decoded by transposed convolutions to 128×128 images. The discriminator receives the spatially expanded text latent alongside image features and outputs a source distribution and a class distribution; wrong images of other classes are used as negatives (paper Figure 2). Class labels are used only as a training signal; trained and evaluated on Oxford-102 flowers.

sources.title: TAC-GAN - Text Conditioned Auxiliary Classifier Generative Adversarial Network

models.name: Text-SeGAN
models.architecture: TAC-GAN variant whose discriminator predicts image source (real/fake) and semantic relevance to the text instead of a class label
models.notes: The generator maps an encoded caption and noise to 64×64 images. Training uses triplets of a positive image, its text encoding and a negative image selected by class and by distance in the text-embedding space (random, easy, hard, semi-easy and semi-hard negatives, plus an easy-to-hard curriculum); the generator maximizes the relevance likelihood while minimizing the source likelihood of fakes (paper Figure 3). The contribution is largely a training strategy on top of the TAC-GAN design. Evaluated on Oxford-102 flowers. No author-linked code repository was found.

sources.title: Adversarial Learning of Semantic Relevance in Text to Image Synthesis

models.name: Text2Scene
models.architecture: Non-adversarial sequence-to-sequence model that places objects one at a time on a canvas, using attention over a bidirectional-GRU text encoding to predict each object and its location and attributes
models.notes: Each step encodes the current canvas with a CNN, updates a convolutional recurrent state, attends over the text to pick the next object, then attends again to predict its location map and attribute maps (paper Figure 2). The same framework outputs cartoon-like Abstract Scenes, COCO object layouts, or synthetic image composites; for composites it also predicts an appearance vector used to retrieve segmented foreground patches from a precomputed collection of training-image segments, and an optional stitching (inpainting) network from prior work fills gaps. The model is not a GAN and does not synthesize pixels from scratch.
models.description: Text2Scene (CVPR 2019) generates scenes from text by predicting a sequence of objects and their attributes instead of synthesizing pixels with a GAN. At each step it attends to different words to decide what to add and where, producing clip-art scenes, object layouts, or photographic composites assembled from retrieved image segments; this makes the output interpretable object by object.

sources.title: Text2Scene: Generating Compositional Scenes from Textual Descriptions

models.name: Transfusion
models.architecture: Single transformer trained with next-token prediction on text tokens and a diffusion objective on continuous VAE latent image patches, with causal attention across the sequence and bidirectional attention within each image
models.description: Transfusion is a training recipe from Meta, Waymo and USC for one multimodal model over discrete and continuous data. A single transformer, trained from scratch, predicts the next token for text and denoises continuous image patches with a diffusion loss in the same sequence, so no image quantization is needed. At inference the model samples text token by token and, on emitting a begin-of-image token, switches to diffusion mode to denoise a block of image patches before returning to text. The paper scales it to 7B parameters on 2T multimodal tokens and reports text-to-image generation, image captioning and text benchmarks from the same model.
models.notes: Images are encoded by a pretrained VAE (an 86M-parameter VAE trained by the authors) into latent patches, which enter the transformer through either a linear layer or U-Net down/up blocks; the U-Net variant lets larger patches be compressed (as few as 16 patches per image). Text and image losses are summed with a balancing coefficient. The paper's controlled comparison against a Chameleon-style discrete-token baseline reports better scaling for text-to-image, image-to-text and text-to-text. A 7B model fine-tuned on about 8k image-editing examples demonstrates text-guided editing; this is a separate fine-tune, so the card is labeled generation. No official weights or code repository were found.

sources.title: Transfusion: Predict the Next Token and Diffuse Images with One Multi-Modal Model

models.name: UFOGen
models.architecture: One-step diffusion-GAN hybrid fine-tuned from Stable Diffusion 1.5, with both the generator and a latent-space discriminator initialized from the pretrained SD U-Net and trained with an adversarial loss on noisy samples plus a reconstruction loss at x0
models.description: UFOGen (Google, 2023) is a one-step text-to-image model that combines diffusion models with a GAN objective. It builds on earlier diffusion-GAN hybrids (DDGAN, SIDDM), which learn large denoising steps adversarially, and modifies the generator parameterization and reconstruction term so that one forward pass from pure noise produces an image. For text-to-image generation, both the generator and the discriminator start from Stable Diffusion 1.5 weights and operate in its latent space, which the paper identifies as key to training a diffusion-GAN at web scale.
models.notes: The generator predicts a clean sample x′0 from x_t; both real and generated samples are diffused to step t−1, where the discriminator compares them, and a reconstruction term λKL·γt·‖x0 − x′0‖² matches clean samples directly (λKL = 1.0). Training uses a denoising step size of 250 on SD's 1000-step schedule, while inference is a single step from x_T. The model keeps SD 1.5's VAE and frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 text encoder (about 0.9B parameters in the network, the same structure as SD). Training data are LAION-Aesthetics-6+, batch size 1024, converging in under 50k steps. The paper also shows image-to-image and controllable generation built on the same model. No code or weights were found.

sources.title: UFOGen: You Forward Once Large Scale Text-to-Image Generation via Diffusion GANs

models.name: UniWorld-V1
models.architecture: Frozen Qwen2.5-VL-7B plus SigLIP2 semantic features, mapped by MLP connectors into the text branch of a FLUX flow-matching diffusion transformer in place of VAE-based reference conditioning
models.description: UniWorld-V1, from Peking University's Yuan group and collaborators, is a unified framework for image understanding, text-to-image generation, image manipulation and image perception tasks such as detection or segmentation rendered as images. Motivated by experiments suggesting that GPT-4o-Image relies on semantic encoders rather than VAEs, it conditions a FLUX diffusion transformer on features from a frozen multimodal LLM (high-level semantics) and from a SigLIP2 encoder (low-level control for reference images). Trained on only 2.7M samples, it is reported to be competitive with BAGEL on image editing benchmarks and scores 0.79 on GenEval.
models.notes: Understanding is performed by the frozen Qwen2.5-VL-7B autoregressively; for generation, reference images pass through both the VLM and SigLIP2-so400m/14 (512 px), and the concatenated features feed FLUX's text branch; the original T5 conditioning is optional (paper Figure 3). Stage 1 trains only the VLM-to-FLUX MLP to align with T5 features; stage 2 initializes the SigLIP MLP from FLUX-Redux and unfreezes the FLUX image branch. An adaptive editing-region weighting emphasizes changed pixels in the loss. The repository notes that the FLUX weights remain under the FLUX.1 [dev] Non-Commercial License. The later UniWorld-V2 (arXiv 2510.16888) is an RL fine-tuning method for editing models and is not covered here.

sources.title: UniWorld-V1: High-Resolution Semantic Encoders for Unified Visual Understanding and Generation

models.name: VILA-U
models.architecture: LLaMA-2-7B autoregressive model over text tokens and residual-quantized visual tokens from a text-aligned SigLIP-based vision tower, with a depth transformer predicting the residual codes at each position
models.description: VILA-U, from Tsinghua, MIT, NVIDIA, UC Berkeley and UC San Diego, is a unified foundation model for video, image and language understanding and generation that uses a single next-token prediction framework without a diffusion model. Its unified vision tower discretizes SigLIP-based vision features with residual quantization and is trained with both image reconstruction and text-image contrastive losses, so the same discrete tokens serve perception and generation. The LLM predicts visual token positions autoregressively while a depth transformer predicts the stacked residual codes, and the RQ-VAE-style decoder turns them back into images or video frames.
models.notes: The vision encoder is SigLIP-Large-patch16-256 or SigLIP-SO400M-patch14-384 with an RQ-VAE quantizer (16,384-entry codebook), giving 16×16×4 codes at 256×256 or 27×27×16 codes at 384×384. Videos are represented as concatenated multi-frame image tokens; training data include [text, image] and [text, video] pairs, and the paper reports both text-to-image and text-to-video generation plus image and video understanding. The Hugging Face collection lists one released checkpoint, vila-u-7b-256; the 384 configuration is described in the paper.

sources.title: VILA-U: a Unified Foundation Model Integrating Visual Understanding and Generation

models.name: VL-GPT
models.architecture: LLaMA-7B transformer trained auto-regressively on interleaved text tokens and continuous visual embeddings (cross-entropy for text, MSE regression for images), with an image tokenizer (frozen CLIP-L plus causal transformer) and detokenizer (transformer decoder plus frozen IP-Adapter Plus diffusion decoder)
models.description: VL-GPT, from Xi'an Jiaotong University, Tencent AI Lab, ARC Lab (Tencent PCG) and HKU, is a generative pretrained transformer for vision-language understanding and generation. Its image tokenizer-detokenizer framework encodes an image into a short sequence of continuous visual embeddings and reconstructs it in pixel space; the embeddings are supervised to carry both image detail and caption semantics. These embeddings and text tokens form one multimodal sequence on which the LLM is trained to predict the next token or embedding, so generated embeddings can be decoded into images. The paper reports captioning, visual question answering, text-to-image generation and in-context multimodal tasks.
models.notes: The tokenizer's visual encoder is CLIP-L and the detokenizer's diffusion decoder uses the U-Net and VAE from IP-Adapter Plus; both stay frozen, and only the causal transformer and transformer decoder are trained. Each image is represented by N = 32 visual embeddings. The full model has about 7.5B parameters, with LoRA used during multimodal pretraining; instruction tuning data include InstructPix2Pix and MagicBrush editing data. The official repository states that the project was terminated and that code and weights will not be released, so the GitHub source contains no implementation.

models.name: Würstchen
models.architecture: Three-stage cascade: a text-conditional ConvNeXt diffusion model generates 16×24×24 semantic latents (Stage C), a latent diffusion U-Net decodes them into VQGAN latents (Stage B), and an f4 VQGAN decoder produces the image (Stage A)
models.notes: Stage C works at a 42:1 spatial compression and is a sequence of 16 ConvNeXt blocks without downsampling, with text and timestep conditioning via cross-attention after each block; it deviates from the U-Net design, whereas Stage B is a 4-stage ConvNeXt U-Net in the unquantized 4×256×256 latent of the Stage A VQGAN, conditioned on text and on the Semantic Compressor latents (paper Sec. 3 and appendix). During training an EfficientNetV2-S Semantic Compressor provides the Stage C targets; it is replaced by Stage C at inference. The paper's model uses an 18M Stage A, 1B Stage B and 1B Stage C, conditioned on un-pooled CLIP-H text embeddings. Stable Cascade (Stability AI, announced 2024-02-12) is built on the Würstchen architecture, with Stage C in 1B and 3.6B and Stage B in 700M and 1.5B sizes; its weights use the non-commercial `stable-cascade-nc-community` license and its code (Stability-AI/StableCascade) is MIT.

sources.title: Wuerstchen: An Efficient Architecture for Large-Scale Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

models.name: X-Omni
models.architecture: Qwen2.5-7B autoregressive model with added vision-specific blocks that predicts discrete SigLIP-VQ semantic image tokens, decoded to pixels by a FLUX.1-dev-based diffusion decoder, with GRPO reinforcement learning
models.description: X-Omni, from Tencent Hunyuan, argues that discrete autoregressive image generation can be competitive again when combined with reinforcement learning. One autoregressive model handles language and images as next-token prediction over text tokens and semantic image tokens from a frozen SigLIP-VQ tokenizer, and an offline diffusion decoder reconstructs pixels from the generated tokens. GRPO with a reward mix of human-preference, unified-reward, VLM-judged text-image alignment and OCR accuracy scores reduces the artifacts that come from the mismatch between generated tokens and the decoder. The paper reports strong instruction following and long-text rendering in English and Chinese, and introduces LongText-Bench.
models.notes: The SigLIP-VQ tokenizer uses a SigLIP2-g ViT with a vector quantizer (16,384 codes, 2,048 dimensions), aligned with Qwen2.5-1.5B on understanding tasks and then frozen. The Qwen2.5-7B base gains four randomly initialized vision-specific transformer blocks before and after the original layers, operating only on image tokens, plus new image embeddings and heads; images are prefixed with height and width tokens and use the LLM's 1D RoPE (paper Section 3.1 and Figure 3). The decoder maps semantic tokens into intermediate features of FLUX.1-dev and is trained for reconstruction. Released checkpoints include English and Chinese text-rendering variants plus pretraining and SFT checkpoints.
